newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan harvest ahead of five-year average.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan harvest ahead of five-year average.

text.p: Combining of spring-seeded crops was ahead of the five-year average with most of the work in the south, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its report.

One percent of spring wheat, durum and oats were combined by Sunday. Two percent of canola and barley were combined. Five percent of spring rye, seven percent of mustard and 26 percent of field peas and lentils were combined.

Scattered showers dropped an average 20 mm (0.8 inch) of rain which should improve yield prospects of late seeded crops. The rain was seen as beneficial to canola but may lead to staining and bleaching of other crops.

The southern grain belt saw hot and dry weather early in the week that continued to cause crop damage followed by an average 15 mm (0.6 inch) of rain. Bertha armyworms, diamond back moth larva, flea beetles and grasshoppers caused crop damage in the southeast and south central regions.

Central Saskatchewan saw dry and hot weather early in the week followed by cooler temperatures and an average 25 mm (1 inch) of rain. Bertha armyworms, diamond back moth larva, flea beetles and grasshoppers caused crop damage.
Northern grainbelt crops saw hot and dry weather early in the week followed by an average 19 mm (0.7 inch) of rain.
Bertha armyworms, diamond back moth larva, flea beetles and grasshoppers caused crop damage in the north central region.
